_meta.indication: EXXUA is indicated for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults.
_meta.receipt_date: October 1, 1999 (original NDA received); resubmission constituting complete response received December 23, 2022

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 134001 (Org 33062 ER in subjects with major depressive disorder)
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 2 or 3 randomized, double-blind controlled study
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled study with flexible-dose titration of gepirone ER 20–80 mg once daily
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 8 in the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) total score
pivotal_trials.result: HAMD-17 LS mean CFB: gepirone ER -9.04 vs placebo -6.75; placebo-subtracted difference -2.47 (95% CI -4.41, -0.53); p=0.013

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study FK-GBE-007 (Org 33062 ER in subjects with major depressive disorder)
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 2 or 3 randomized, double-blind controlled study
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled study with flexible-dose titration of gepirone ER 20–80 mg daily
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 8 in the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) total score
pivotal_trials.result: HAMD-17 LS mean CFB: gepirone ER -10.22 vs placebo -7.96; placebo-subtracted difference -2.45 (95% CI -4.47, -0.43); p=0.018

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and twice placebo): dizziness (49% vs 10% placebo), nausea (35% vs 13%), insomnia (14% vs 5%), abdominal pain (7% vs 3%), and dyspepsia (6% vs 2%). Key serious risks include QT prolongation, serotonin syndrome, and activation of mania/hypomania.
target_moa: Gepirone is a selective partial agonist at serotonergic (5-HT1A) receptors; a new molecular entity whose mechanism of action is similar to buspirone.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS — antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients in short-term studies; closely monitor all antidepressant-treated patients. EXXUA is not approved for use in pediatric patients.

advisory_committee.vote: A Psychopharmacological Drug Advisory Committee (PDAC) met December 1, 2015: of the 13-member committee, 9 did not agree the Applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness and 9 did not agree there was a favorable benefit-risk profile, though 11 members agreed safety was adequately characterized. No advisory committee was convened for the current resubmission.

summary.text: EXXUA (gepirone ER) is a new molecular entity approved under a traditional 505(b) NDA for MDD in adults. The original NDA was received October 1, 1999 and had a long history of non-approvals; substantial evidence of effectiveness (two positive short-term studies, 134001 and FK-GBE-007) was established through a dispute-resolution appeal granted March 16, 2016, and the NDA was resubmitted December 23, 2022. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designations are documented; postmarketing requirements include pregnancy studies, a lactation study, and a thorough QT/QTc study.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated September 30, 1999, received October 1, 1999, and your amendments, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Exxua (gepirone) extended-release tablets.
During a dispute resolution process initiated by the Applicant, FDA determined that these two positive adequate and well-controlled studies provided substantial evidence of effectiveness.
